title: Journey of a River
seo_title: Journey of a River Class 5 EVS Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 2)
standard_code: Class 5, Our Wondrous World Chapter 2: Journey of a River
standard_text: The journey of a river from its source in the mountains to its mouth at the sea; parts of a river; important rivers of India; how rivers support plants, animals, people and culture; how human activities pollute rivers and ways to protect them (summary of NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 2).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 5 EVS worksheets for NCERT Our Wondrous World Chapter 2: a river's journey, parts of a river, rivers of India, dams, deltas, river life and keeping rivers clean. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A river flows from the mountains to the sea.
key_sub: Rivers give us water, food, soil and travel.
body_html:
How to think about it

A river begins at its source, a glacier or spring in the mountains. It rushes down steep valleys, slows and bends (meanders) across the flat plains, is joined by tributaries and finally meets the sea at its mouth, often building a delta. The Ganga begins at Gangotri and reaches the Bay of Bengal through the Sundarbans delta.

Rivers give water, fish, fertile soil and transport, so cities grew along them. Garbage, factory waste and sewage pollute rivers and harm animals such as the Ganges river dolphin. Planting trees on banks and treating waste water keep rivers healthy.

Example

A smaller river joining a bigger one is…

the Yamuna joins the Ganga

Answer: a tributary

Example

Where a river meets the sea is…

end of the journey

Answer: its mouth

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a river's source is at the sea.
  • Mixing up a delta and a tributary.
  • Thinking rivers can clean any amount of waste.
